name: labelImg
product: LabelImg, originally developed by TzuTa Lin and archived by HumanSignal

evidence.says: The archived project says development ended and documents macOS use via Python or a locally packaged py2app bundle.
The maintainer’s final PyPI release, 1.8.6, was published October 11, 2021 and contains a source archive.

limitation: No official native macOS binary was established for the final version, and the architecture of locally packaged copies can vary.
notes: The project directs users to Label Studio.

name: Xournal++
product: Xournal++ by the Xournal++ project

evidence.says: The official project download page offers separate stable ARM and Intel Mac builds of version 1.3.8.
The official release list dates the 1.3.8 macOS ARM64 DMG to September 26, 2026.
The project documents a macOS code-signing issue that can block the released app at launch.

notes: The project documents a Gatekeeper workaround for the downloaded Mac builds.

name: TNEF's Enough
product: TNEF's Enough for macOS by Josh Jacob

evidence.says: Josh Jacob offers 3.9 as the current Mac release and lists 3.8 under legacy versions.
The developer explicitly identifies 3.9 as a universal binary for Intel and Apple Silicon.
Apple dates the Mac App Store release of version 3.9 for com.joshjacob.TNEFsEnough to September 11, 2026.

notes: The supplied Homebrew hint refers to the older 3.8 release.

name: Badlion Client
product: Standalone Badlion Client Minecraft launcher, now owned by Moonsworth

evidence.says: Badlion's official Mac download now delivers Lunar Client and directs users to launch Badlion through it.
Moonsworth documents the migration of Badlion into the unified Lunar Client Launcher.
The cask for the former standalone app lists a versioned 4.5.4 arm64 DMG from Badlion's update server.

limitation: An arm64 standalone release is documented for 4.5.4, but the final standalone Mac version and its architecture were unverified.
notes: The listing covers the standalone launcher bundle. Badlion services continue inside Lunar Client.

name: owncloud
product: ownCloud Desktop App by ownCloud (Kiteworks)

evidence.says: The vendor lists v7.1.1 as a September 1, 2026 release with a separate macOS Apple Silicon package.
The vendor's release tag confirms the exact Desktop App release.

name: FINAL FANTASY XIV ONLINE
product: FINAL FANTASY XIV ONLINE Mac client by Square Enix

evidence.says: Square Enix distributes the official 64-bit Mac client as FINAL_FANTASY_XIV_ONLINE_x64.dmg.
Square Enix lists supported Apple Silicon Macs and explicitly requires Rosetta on them.

limitation: Square Enix does not publish a launcher version number on its download page.

name: FlowJo
product: FlowJo flow cytometry analysis software by FlowJo, LLC (BD)

evidence.says: The vendor offers distinct M-series and Intel macOS downloads for FlowJo 11.2 and links to the maintained version 10 branch.
The release notes date FlowJo 11.2 to May 29, 2026.

limitation: The architecture claim covers the 11.2 M-series download only.
notes: The existing listing came from version 10.8.1, and the vendor distributes the version 10 and 11 branches separately.

name: CPLEX Optimization Studio 22.1
product: IBM ILOG CPLEX Optimization Studio 22.1.0 InstallAnywhere installer for macOS

evidence.says: The scan’s Info.plist ties this exact identifier to Flexera InstallAnywhere and names the InstallAnywhere installer entry point.
IBM identifies release 22.1.0 as IBM ILOG CPLEX Optimization Studio and provides version-specific macOS installation guidance.

notes: The scanned bundle was the distribution installer rather than the CPLEX IDE or optimizer.

name: WD Drive Utilities Installer
product: Western Digital WD Drive Utilities Installer for macOS

evidence.says: Western Digital tells users to launch WD Drive Utilities Installer from the disk image to install the separate WD Drive Utilities application.

notes: The scan used the installer bundle identifier and also recorded an uninstaller under this listing.

name: Jumpcloud
product: JumpCloud Agent menu-bar tray by JumpCloud

evidence.says: JumpCloud lists com.jumpcloud.jcagent-tray.plist as a persistent login item installed with the JumpCloud Agent.
The Agent's macOS installation inventory identifies the menu-bar tray as part of the JumpCloud Agent and lists its log directory.

notes: The scanned bundle is the Agent's tray component and ships as part of the managed-device Agent package.

name: Universal Presenter Remote
product: Universal Presenter Remote Desktop by DBZ Technology

evidence.says: The vendor's Mac control software download points to the version 2.0.7 universal macOS DMG.
The developer's July 8, 2026 release lists universal Mac DMG and ZIP builds for version 2.0.7.
The developer documents upgrades from legacy 1.3.x and identifies the desktop app ID preserved across releases as com.universalpresenterremote.desktop.

notes: The desktop control software is distributed separately from the phone and watch remote.

name: GLMv4
product: Genelec Loudspeaker Manager (GLM) 4 by Genelec

evidence.says: Genelec's regional download page still provides GLM 4.2.2 and lists Rosetta mode for Apple Silicon.
Genelec's November 4 release notes identify Intel and Rosetta support for the GLM 4.2.2 application with Cloud AutoCal2.
The separate GLM 5.2.0 release is listed as a Universal Binary.

limitation: Genelec documents Apple Silicon compatibility for macOS 11 through 12.0 with Cloud AutoCal2. Local AutoCal and newer macOS releases are outside that statement.
notes: The listing identifies GLM 4. The newer GLM 5 major version has a native Apple Silicon build.

name: PureRef
product: PureRef by Idyllic Pixel

evidence.says: PureRef's changelog dates 2.1.4 to November 15, 2026 and records the switch to a universal Apple Silicon and Intel app in 2.1.2.
The official macOS download serves PureRef-2.1.4_x64.dmg, whose PureRef.app/Contents/MacOS/PureRef executable is a universal x86_64 and arm64 Mach-O and whose bundle ID matches the scan.

notes: The vendor's DMG filename contains x64. The inspected app contains both architectures.

name: Accountable2You
product: Accountable2You monitoring app for Mac by Accountable2You

evidence.says: The vendor's Mac installation guide offers separate downloads for Apple Silicon and Intel.
The official Apple Silicon package identifies Accountable2You 6.4.11 in PackageInfo and its main Accountable2You.app/Contents/MacOS/accountable2you executable is Mach-O arm64.

limitation: The package does not give a release date.
notes: The current package identifies its app as com.accountable2you.agent. The scan used the earlier com.icnventures.accountable2you bundle ID.

name: Sol Client
product: Sol Client’s Electron launcher for Minecraft Java Edition by the Sol Client project

evidence.says: The developer archived the project on July 2, 2023 and describes retiring the Electron launcher.
GitHub’s official release record lists the December 31, 2022 Sol Client 1.8.9 Mac disk image as x64, with no arm64 Mac asset.

notes: The final Mac download was Intel x64. The developer moved on to Axolotl Client.

name: MQTT Explorer
product: MQTT Explorer by Thomas Nordquist

evidence.says: The project’s current macOS download offers separate ARM and Intel builds of 0.4.0-beta.6.
This is the official prerelease page for MQTT Explorer 0.4.0-beta.6.
The official release metadata lists the arm64 Mac DMG and May 15, 2024 publication date for 0.4.0-beta.6.

limitation: The official ARM download is a beta and the evidence does not apply to the older 0.3.5 stable build.
notes: The beta is linked from the main vendor download page.

name: Live Home 3D Pro
product: BeLight Software Live Home 3D Pro, Mac App Store edition

evidence.says: Apple’s catalog metadata matches the scanned bundle ID and dates the Mac App Store release of 5.1.2 to November 5, 2026.
BeLight lists Apple silicon and Intel processors for Live Home 3D Pro 5.1.2 and links its Mac App Store edition.
BeLight’s macOS release history records the addition of native Apple Silicon support in the product line.

notes: The exact Mac App Store bundle is distinct from the separately listed iOS edition.

name: Spectacle
product: Spectacle window manager by Eric Czarny

evidence.says: The archived project explicitly says that Spectacle is no longer maintained, with downloads still available.
The official release metadata gives January 15, 2022 and links the 1.2 ZIP.
Inspection of Spectacle.app/Contents/MacOS/Spectacle in the official 1.2 ZIP found only x86_64, and the app manifest matches the scanned bundle ID.

notes: The final official Mac release is Intel-only. The original site domain has been superseded as a download source by the project repository.

name: Tutanota Desktop
product: Tuta Mail desktop client by Tutao GmbH, formerly Tutanota Desktop

evidence.says: Tutao's stable desktop release lists the official Mac DMG and a publication date of November 24, 2026.
The versioned official build pipeline builds the Mac release with the universal architecture flag.
The versioned publishing pipeline maps the Mac build to the exact tutanota-desktop-mac.dmg release asset.
Tutao's versioned packaging template retains bundle ID de.tutao.tutanota and describes merging x64 and arm64 Mac builds.

notes: The Mac executable is named Tuta Mail in the package template.

name: Meld
product: GNOME Meld visual diff and merge tool, packaged for macOS by René de Hesselle

evidence.says: The upstream project points Mac users to semi-official builds rather than distributing a first-party macOS binary.
The maintainer of that macOS packaging project dates this release to March 3, 2025 and supplies separate arm64 and x86_64 DMG assets.
The current Homebrew cask selects the René de Hesselle 3.22.3+105 Apple Silicon build.

limitation: GNOME describes macOS builds as semi-official.
notes: This release is from the Mac packaging project, which is distinct from GNOME's upstream version numbering.

name: Disk Analyzer Pro
product: Disk Analyzer Pro for Mac by Systweak Software

evidence.says: Systweak identifies the Mac disk space analyzer and distributes it through the Mac App Store.
Apple's catalog API matches the scanned bundle ID and gives version 4.7.0 with a November 4, 2026 release date.

limitation: The vendor and Apple's catalog do not state the current Mac binary's architecture.

name: Autenticação.gov
product: Autenticação.gov desktop application by Portugal's government digital-services agency (ARTE, formerly AMA)

evidence.says: The Portuguese government offers version 3.16.1 as the current macOS download.
The official installer contains bundle pt.gov.autenticacao version 3.16.1, whose Contents/MacOS/eidguiV2 is x86_64 only.
The agency's release notes identify October 29, 2026 as the 3.16.1 macOS installer update and say it has no functional changes from 3.16.0.
The agency maintainer says the 3.16 Mac build works on macOS 27 with Rosetta and describes the native port as future work.

name: MDB ACCDB Viewer
product: MDB ACCDB Viewer (direct edition) by Jakob Egger / Egger Apps

evidence.says: Egger Apps lists 2.3.2 in its changelog and documents the move to a universal Apple Silicon and Intel binary in 2.3.
The developer-hosted 2.3.2 archive contains at.eggerapps.mdbviewer, and inspection of MDB ACCDB Viewer.app/Contents/MacOS/MDB ACCDB Viewer Direct found x86_64 and arm64 slices.
The App Store channel lists 2.3.3, while the inspected developer-hosted direct build is 2.3.2.

limitation: Binary inspection covers the exact direct edition in the scan.
notes: The vendor's main page now directs purchases to the Mac App Store.

name: Gas Mask
product: Gas Mask macOS hosts-file manager by Clockwise, published by 2ndalpha

evidence.says: The project still points users to 0.8.6 as its latest stable download.
The tagged release provides gas_mask_0.8.6.zip, whose Gas Mask.app/Contents/MacOS/Gas Mask main executable was inspected and contains only an x86_64 slice.
Two users report the app works on M1 Pro Macs running Monterey, and the original reporter subsequently confirmed it was usable after making the menu-bar icon visible.

limitation: Successful user reports are for Monterey, and current macOS Gatekeeper behavior was untested.
notes: The project's source tree includes ARM build work, while the published 0.8.6 ZIP is Intel-only.

name: PdaNetMac
product: PdaNet+ USB Desktop Client for Mac by June Fabrics Technology

evidence.says: June Fabrics offers the 5.01 USB client for macOS 10.14 and 10.15 and lists a separate Wi-Fi Direct client.
Inspection of PdaNetMac.app/Contents/MacOS/PdaNetMac (bundle com.jft.pdanet, version 5.01) and PdaNetDrv.kext/Contents/MacOS/PdaNetDrv in the official package found x86_64 only in both.
Apple states that Rosetta does not translate kernel extensions, so the inspected USB driver cannot load on Apple Silicon.

limitation: The unsupported result applies to USB tethering with the scanned client bundle.
notes: The vendor's 5.24 Wi-Fi Direct client is a separate download.

name: Envy
product: Envy 2 standalone sound-design app by The Cargo Cult

evidence.says: The Cargo Cult lists 2.2.2 as its current Envy 2 macOS download.
The Envy changelog records Apple Silicon support entering the Envy 2 series in version 2.1.2 and lists 2.2.2 as the latest update.
The vendor’s linked manual identifies standalone Envy 2 version 2.1.7 as universal for Apple Silicon and Intel.

limitation: The vendor confirms a universal 2.1.7 build, but does not specify the architecture of 2.2.2 and its 340 MB archive exceeds the inspection limit.
notes: The listing covers the standalone Envy editor used with DAWs.

name: AppZapper
product: AppZapper 2 by Austin Sarner and Brian Ball

evidence.says: The original product’s vendor download endpoint redirects to AppZapper 2.0.5.
Inspection of AppZapper.app/Contents/MacOS/AppZapper in the official 2.0.5 ZIP found arm64 and x86_64, and the manifest matches the scanned bundle ID.
The vendor’s main site now promotes the rebuilt AppZapper 3000.

notes: AppZapper 3000 has a separate bundle identifier (com.appzapper.appzapper3000). The vendor still serves the matching AppZapper 2 ZIP.

name: Speedify
product: Speedify bonding VPN by Connectify

evidence.says: Connectify’s November 10, 2026 release announcement identifies Speedify 17.3 and its macOS changes.
Inspection of Speedify.app/Contents/MacOS/Speedify Network Extension in the official 17.3.0 build 4125 DMG found x86_64 and arm64 and confirmed the scanned bundle ID.

notes: The release date is for the 17.3 release announcement.

name: SamsungPortableSSD
product: Samsung Portable SSD Software for T5, X5 and earlier drives by Samsung Electronics

evidence.says: Samsung still distributes the 1.6.10 legacy-drive Mac installer and also offers its newer Magician utility.

The official archive's universal installer branch contains com.samsung.portablessd.software 1.6.10.1, whose SamsungPortableSSD.app/Contents/MacOS/SamsungPortableSSD executable has arm64 and x86_64 slices.

limitation: Binary inspection establishes the main application's architecture. Drive-specific features and driver loading were untested.
notes: The same archive has an Intel-only branch with the identical bundle ID and version, which explains why the version number alone cannot identify the architecture.

name: KeyboardLock
product: Keyboard Lock macOS bundle com.virae.Keyboard-Lock, publisher unverified

evidence.says: The historical scan identifies an application bundle named KeyboardLock with executable Keyboard Lock and version 1.0.

limitation: No current release, developer page, or architecture information could be tied to this bundle ID.

name: ArtNetView
product: ArtNetView by Haute Technique B.V.

evidence.says: Haute Technique names 2.2.1 as the current ArtNetView version and directs its Mac download to the App Store.
Apple's US catalog identifies the exact bundle ID but returns version 2.1, without an architecture field.
The historical scan identifies the exact 2.2.1 bundle as x86.

limitation: The vendor's current download points to a different version, so the historical 2.2.1 scan does not verify the architecture of the build now delivered to Mac users.

name: AQ Device Manager
product: AudioQuest Desktop Device Manager by AudioQuest / The Quest Group

evidence.says: AudioQuest identifies the Desktop Device Manager as its firmware utility for selected DragonFly and Beetle hardware.
The historical scan identifies version 1.1 of the exact bundle as x86.
The download address given in the DragonFly manuals now redirects to the AudioQuest homepage.

limitation: A current official build, its architecture, and any formal end-of-support notice could not be verified.
notes: Compatibility of the DragonFly DAC hardware does not establish compatibility of the updater.

name: DAEMON Tools
product: DAEMON Tools for Mac by Disc Soft Ltd.

evidence.says: The official update feed identifies build 8.6.793 and dates it to September 27, 2023.
Inspection of the official DAEMONTools-8-6-793.dmg found a universal x86_64 and arm64 main executable at DAEMON Tools.app/Contents/MacOS/DAEMON Tools with the matching app bundle ID.
Disc Soft documents additional installation steps for the Mac app on ARM-based devices.

notes: The app's short version is 8.6 and Disc Soft's public release notes call it 8.6.0.

name: Air Video Server HD
product: Air Video Server HD for macOS by InMethod s.r.o.

evidence.says: The vendor's product page identifies the Mac server download separately from the mobile player.
The vendor-linked installer resolves to version 2.3.0-beta1u1, whose matching bundle has an x86_64-only main executable at Air Video Server HD.app/Contents/MacOS/AirVideoServerHD.
Homebrew's cask identifies the same version as requiring Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon.
MacUpdater records February 18, 2018 as the release date for this exact Intel Mac server version.

limitation: Current macOS runtime compatibility was not tested.
notes: The mobile Air Video HD player is separate from the Mac server.

name: JEDict
product: JEDict 5 for Mac by Sergey Kurkin

evidence.says: The developer explicitly says JEDict 5 is no longer supported and explains that JEDict 6 is a separate app that can coexist with it.
The archived Mac listing identifies JEDict 5.0.4 as 32-bit Intel and PowerPC and reports incompatibility with macOS Catalina or later.

limitation: The architecture of 5.0.4 is documented by the archive and was not independently inspected.
notes: The Apple App Store's current same-name listing should not supply compatibility for the retired JEDict 5 bundle.

name: iMyFone Fixppo
product: iMyFone Fixppo for Mac by iMyFone

evidence.says: The vendor offers Fixppo as an iOS repair utility with a Mac download.
Inspection of iMyFone Fixppo.app/Contents/MacOS/iMyFone Fixppo in the vendor’s DMG found x86_64 only and matched the original bundle ID and version 9.3.7.1.

limitation: No vendor statement or credible hands-on report confirmed Rosetta operation for this build.
notes: The DMG contains the actual application. The separate ZIP linked by the product page contains a distinct installer bundle.

name: Any Video Converter
product: Any Video Converter for Mac by Anvsoft

evidence.says: The vendor’s Mac release notes date version 9.2.6 to September 29, 2026.
Anvsoft lists Intel and Apple Silicon for basic Mac operation without naming the app’s executable architecture.
Inspection of Any Video Converter Installer.app/Contents/MacOS/Any Video Converter Installer found an x86_64 installer at version 1.2.0 with the separate com.anvsoft.avc.installer identifier.

limitation: The architecture of the installed 9.2.6 converter could not be verified from the documentation or the installer-only download.
notes: The alternate disk image for older macOS versions exceeds the brief’s 150 MB inspection limit.

name: Wondershare UniConverter 13
product: Wondershare UniConverter 13 for Mac, international edition by Wondershare

evidence.says: The vendor's catalog lists 13.6.8 as the latest Mac release for the UniConverter 13 product code, with a single platform 4 package still available.
The same vendor catalog maps Mac platform 4 to the standard Intel package and platform 3 to the explicitly ARM-labeled download for newer versions.
Homebrew corroborates the newer vendor package naming by using the ARM-labeled URL for Apple Silicon and the other URL for Intel.
The vendor's international Mac release history introduces native Apple Silicon support in 14.2.0.

limitation: The vendor's platform metadata identifies one Intel build for 13.6.8, but Rosetta evidence for that exact release was not found and the full binary exceeded the inspection limit.
notes: Homebrew's current cask tracks the international version 18 product. This record covers the explicitly versioned UniConverter 13 listing.

name: Wondershare UniConverter
product: Wondershare UniConverter for Mac, Chinese edition (万兴优转)

evidence.says: Wondershare identifies 万兴优转 as the Chinese-market UniConverter product.
The official Chinese Mac product page advertises Apple Silicon support and supplies the installer for product code 4982.
The Chinese product's live release catalog lists version 14.1.2 with separate ARM and standard ZIP packages.
The vendor's full versioned ARM download responded successfully and reports a March 25, 2026 UTC modification date matching the release metadata.

notes: The vendor catalog entry's headline says 14.1.3, but its version field and working ARM package both say 14.1.2. Homebrew tracks the international edition, which has separate version numbering.

name: Maxon Chromatic Displacement
product: Maxon App, the installation and licensing manager by Maxon Computer GmbH

evidence.says: The historical scan records Maxon App as the bundle name and net.maxon.app-manager as the bundle identifier.
Maxon dates the 2027.1.0 app release to November 23, 2026.
Inspection of Maxon.app/Contents/MacOS/Maxon from the installer payload found x86_64 and arm64 slices and confirmed the net.maxon.app-manager bundle and version 2027.1.0.

notes: Retitle this record to Maxon App. The existing title describes a separate Red Giant effect.
